_provenance.source: Hand-transcribed from the reference design image (image.png at the repo root). NOT captured: test/visual/capture.mjs only produces b-fresh, c-native and e-full.
_provenance.shape: Mirrors protocol.ts's DashboardData, but every value is the reference's or invented to draw it — it is not what a project on disk produced.
transcribed-from-the-image: version "1.8.4" — the reference footer's text. The footer names the Avenic CLI the reader is actually running (panel.ts passes cachedAvenicCliVersion()), and the CLI this repo produces is 1.8.4, so the string here is the shape a real host emits; the digits pin the build, not the machine's own answer
versionDetails.cli "1.8.4" / .extension "0.6.0" — the footer's title tooltip, composed from the same two answers a host passes; nothing measures it, because no reference box shows a tooltip

project {"signal-desk"} — invented for this derived fixture, as are the shared and native session rows, the activity rows and all 120 transcript turns. The reference's own project is not this file's, and no value here comes from a project on disk
_provenance.invented-to-draw-the-reference: agents[].fields values and options, skills and pack names, hub spec/revision — carried over from the reference payload; the rows, activity and transcript named above are added by this fixture, which exists because it is the one payload whose conversation (120 turns) is longer than the browser's own newest-100 window, so both panes' scrollers and the panes' height are drawn from content rather than from three rows that happen to fit
_provenance.gated-by: shot.mjs renders this payload; compare.mjs measures it against fixtures/reference-geometry.json, whose refs come from the image itself (e.g. text.version's 74..151px run). The footer's text is gated as a pattern — "Avenic v" and a dotted number — never by those digits, which are live machine data
_provenance.not-regenerated: capture.mjs never writes this file, so a value here that the host cannot emit stays until someone decides what the footer should show

agents.label: OpenCode
agents.detail: OpenCode manages its own provider, authentication and model configuration. Avenic does not modify them.

rows.title: Keep the ledger write behind the drain
Drain order, read from the ledger

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Why does the queue drain before the first write lands?

turns.speaker: Claude
turns.text: The drain reads the ledger once, so the write that follows it is the one that queues.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can the desk keep two readers on the same ticket?

turns.speaker: Codex
turns.text: It can, but only if both readers take the same ticket snapshot.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Which pass decides the reply order?

turns.speaker: OpenCode
turns.text: The second pass sorts by arrival, then by the ledger line the desk wrote.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Does the retry keep the original arrival time?

turns.speaker: Claude
turns.text: Yes — the arrival time is carried on the batch, not recomputed on retry.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: What happens when a batch is half acknowledged?

turns.speaker: Codex
turns.text: The unacknowledged half is re-offered on the next pass, not dropped.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Should the backlog be measured in items or in seconds?

turns.speaker: OpenCode
turns.text: In seconds: an item count hides the case where one item is very slow.
